title: Cross-cycle Capacity Signals and Surge Handoff
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As Redwood scales, we repeatedly see mid-cycle shocks where demand growth, large enterprise onboarding, or infra incidents create urgent capacity needs. These events force ad-hoc staffing moves, scope cuts, and reactive rollouts. The current process for surfacing capacity pressure and executing a surge is informal: slack posts, individual manager escalation, and manual spreadsheet updates. This leads to uneven outcomes across initiatives and burnout for on-call engineers.

Objective: Define a repeatable cross-cycle signal taxonomy, a lightweight handoff protocol for surge activation, and a small set of tooling changes (dashboards + runbooks) so product, engineering, and GTM can make consistent staffing and scope decisions with clear ownership. This ticket scopes the process definition, minimal UI/alert changes, and a pilot in Cycle 41.

What success looks like (acceptance criteria):
- A published "Cross-cycle Capacity Signal Guide" (confluence) describing signal thresholds, roles, and handoff steps.
- Two alerts wired into the Cycle Capacity dashboard: (1) Trailing 7-day throughput vs baseline spike > 40% and (2) OKR progress velocity falling > 20% behind plan while burn rate is high.
- A documented surge activation play (Slack channel, on-call rotation, PM triage cadence) tested in a tabletop drill.
- Pilot run for one mid-sized initiative during Cycle 41 with measured reduction in ad-hoc calls-to-action and a post-mortem.

Proposed signal taxonomy (examples):
- Usage velocity: 7d and 30d token/req growth vs expected baseline per initiative; threshold: 40% sustained for >72h.
- Capacity runway: Estimated GPU-hours left for Dedicated pools vs forecasted consumption for next 14 days; threshold: <25% runway.
- Quality outage/reliability signal: Error rate > 1.5x baseline for 6+ hours or increasing request latency P95 > SLA target.
- OKR momentum signal: Feature-level completion velocity compared to plan; threshold: 20% behind on committed scope for two checkpoints.

Handoff protocol (high level):
1) Signal detection: alert posted to #capacity-signals with automated summary + link to Matrix row.
2) Initial triage (15m): PM, Eng lead, SRE rep acknowledge. Determine if this is (A) self-remediable, (B) capacity surge required, or (C) scope freeze/rollback.
3) Surge activation: if (B), create Surge ticket (ENG-) and assign surge captain; notify staffing roster and spin up temporary pairing with Dedicated ops.
4) Scope decision: PMs post proposed scope-reduction options and impact on OKRs; leadership approves cut/deferral within 2 triage windows.
5) Closure and learnings: collect metrics and short post-mortem within 5 business days.

Roles and responsibilities:
- PM (assignee): owns prioritization and public communication to stakeholders.
- Eng lead: drafts surge mitigation plan (short-term capacity, batching/quantization knobs).
- SRE/Infra: provides runway numbers and capacity adjustments.
- Ops/Capacity on-call: executes Dedicated pool changes and monitoring.

Tooling changes (minimum viable):
- Cycle Capacity Matrix: a single spreadsheet row per initiative showing expected vs actual throughput, runway, and OKR velocity.
- Two alert rules implemented in observability (alerts link to Cycle Capacity Matrix).
- Slack templates for triage and surge announcement.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Too many false positives from noisy signals. Mitigation: add hysteresis (sustained windows) and require confirmation from infra metrics before surge activation.
- Risk: Surge fatigue. Mitigation: cap surge activations per initiative per quarter and rotate surge captains.

Timeline / milestones:
- Week 1 (2025-02-03 to 2025-02-09): Draft signal taxonomy and handoff protocol; share with Eng and SRE for feedback.
- Week 2 (2025-02-10 to 2025-02-16): Implement two alert rules and wire to Cycle Capacity Matrix; create Slack templates.
- Week 3 (2025-02-17 to 2025-02-23): Tabletop drill with PM/Eng/SRE; adjust playbook.
- Week 4 (pilot): Activate pilot on one initiative and collect data.

Metrics to track post-pilot: average time from alert to decision, number of ad-hoc staff reshuffles avoided, percentage of scope cuts made with leader approval, and team satisfaction (pulse survey).

Links & artifacts:
- Draft Capacity Signal Guide (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.example/capacity-signal-guide (draft)
- Cycle Capacity Matrix (Sheet): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/cc-cycle-matrix (sheet link)
- Prototype alert PR (observability): https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1421

Notes: This ticket is deliberately scoped to process + light tooling. Deeper investments (automated staffing recommendations, capacity safety buffers in quota management) should be captured as follow-up epics if the pilot demonstrates value.
